cases.name: Natalie Jane Martin
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "She was a Philo High School graduate, Class of 2023. Natalie lived her life to the fullest with joy, laughter, and love. She brought true happiness to all that knew her. She had a free, pure and wild spirit with a contagious laugh, a personality out of this world that could bring anyone out of their darkest of days. Natalie enjoyed all of nature’s beauty. She loved to hunt, shoot guns, fish, wrangle snakes, plant and nurture flowers, and could gut and skin a deer better than most grown men. Natalie spent much time loving on her dogs, Radar, Hella, and Tiny Little B, her many chickens, and her cat, Phoebe. She had a life-long love for softball and soccer. Natalie’s beauty shined like a ray of sunlight and her smile could brighten a whole room. Her glowing blonde hair and beautiful blue eyes represented that she was truly an angel here on Earth.

Natalie previously worked at Northstar Pizza and was currently working for the Sundale Kids as a childcare provider. She formed many special bonds with all the precious little ones she cared for."

cases.name: Wanda "Gail" Ayers Lowry
cases.about:
Family statement:

"With a heavy heart we grieve the tragic and senseless loss of our beloved mother, grandmother, friend and co-worker, Gail.

My mother was a kind and loving person who cared for those around her. She was generous and thoughtful, quick witted and loyal. Without hesitation, she opened her home to a co-worker she believed was a good person going through a bad time. Tragically, my mother’s generosity allowed this horrific man to commit the most heinous and cowardly of acts - this man shot and killed my 74-year old mother in her own home.

She has been taken away from us far too soon and in a manner so terrifying and cruel that our family will never fully recover. We are taught that to be generous and trusting are positive traits. However, we must also be taught to be vigilant and careful. No family should ever have to endure something like this. Such a senseless and painful tragedy.

Hug your loved ones. Life is precious and fragile. My mother will be dearly missed. My family and I thank you for the outpouring of love and support. We also thank the efforts of the Horry County police. During this difficult time we ask for privacy please."
cases.relationship: Coworker / employee / employer; Landlord / neighbor / roommate / tenant
cases.narrative:
On 9/20/2024, Horry County police found her body.

The coroner’s office believes Lowry was killed on Sept. 12 but she wasn’t discovered until Sept. 20 when Horry County police performed a welfare check at her home on Breakers Drive.
